title: Sovereign Deployment: Battlecard & Field Guide for Regulated Buyers
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight but pragmatic battlecard + field guide aimed at sellers, solutions engineers, and partner reps working regulated buyers (finance, healthcare, public sector). It translates technical controls into procurement-friendly language, pre-bakes rebuttals for common objections, and provides a minimal pilot checklist that preserves auditability and evidence for security teams.

TL;DR (elevator to execs):
- We offer a 'sovereign deployment' path where the customer retains network and key custody while Redwood operates a customer-dedicated inference control plane (optionally fully customer-managed).
- Value props to emphasize: predictable latency/throughput for production, deterministic data boundaries, clear audit trail for regulators, and rollback/escape hatches to known-good models.
- Ask: pilot with a scoped workload (PII-free or redacted) + 6-week technical proof-of-evidence; escalate to contract after SLOs and evidence review.

Buyer personas & top concerns (how to frame):
- CISO/Audit: data lineage, audit trail, KMS/HSM integration, evidence for third-party assessments. Use: "We keep an immutable audit stream and hand over logs in standard formats for your SIEM. Keys can stay in your KMS/HSM; Redwood never persistently decrypts customer data outside your boundary."
- Cloud/Infra Architect: network topology, egress minimization, performance (latency and throughput). Use: "We deploy into your VPC or on-prem cluster; traffic stays on private fabric and can be pinned to specific regions/hardware to meet latency SLOs."
- Legal/Privacy: data residency, subprocessor controls, breach notification timelines. Use: "We accept contractual residency constraints and provide a subprocessor list and commitments to notify within X hours for incidents."
- Product/Platform Owner: deterministic inference economics and model governance. Use: "Rollouts, version pinning, and automated fallback keep your feature resilient while tracking per-route cost and token consumption."

Three-tier objection handling (short scripts):
1) "We can’t allow a 3rd party control plane":
  - Quick buyer language: "Control plane can be run in your VPC or under our managed offering; both allow you to keep custody of keys and logs. We can sign controls for visibility and support an offline evidence handover process."
  - Tech translation for SEs: Map to a deployment diagram (customer VPC, private control endpoint, operator jumpbox, optional air-gapped CI). Show where secrets live and where telemetry flows.

2) "We require formal FedRAMP / SOC2 / ISO evidence":
  - Quick buyer language: "We provide SOC2 Type II reports for the hosted plane; for private deployments we provide logs and an 'evidence binder' (standardized artifacts + runbook steps) to support your audit."
  - SE play: offer a Scope + Evidence worksheet during pilot. Attach samples from CONFS-1123.

3) "We’re worried about vendor lock / escape":
  - Quick buyer language: "We commit to clear export formats for model artifacts and state; you can run a compatible runtime locally. We also support automated export of model versions and KV caches for portability."
  - Negotiation lever: add rollback/fallback clauses and a migration assistance SLA in the contract.

Competitive framing (short notes sellers can use):
- Big cloud managed endpoints (AWS Sagemaker, GCP Vertex, Azure OpenAI): they offer convenience but usually centralize control and telemetry. Counter: emphasize predictable, model-level economics and per-route observability + our ability to run entirely inside customer network.
- Inference vendors (self-host runtimes + orchestration): they may claim more control but often lack an evidence-first audit package and commercial SLAs. Counter: point to our battle-tested evidence binder and standardized pilot that maps to auditors' needs.
- Pure SaaS LLM APIs: low friction but fail on data residency and deterministic performance. Counter: pitch hybrid — start hosted for speed, graduate to private for regulated parts.

Technical translation checklist for SEs to bring into calls (one-pagers):
- Identity & keys: who manages KMS/HSM? (customer preferred).
- Network topology: allowlist IPs vs private VPC peering vs Direct Connect.
- Telemetry: which logs are required by customer SIEM (raw vs obfuscated)? retention windows?
- Auditability: hash chains, immutable append logs, signed checkpoints.
- Performance targets: P95 latency, sustained throughput, burst allowances.
- Dataflow diagram: define ingress, inference, egress, and optional cache persistence.
- Backup & escape: automated export cadence for models and KV cache, manual runbook for full handover.

Pilot (6-week) minimal plan (field version):
Week 0: Kickoff, NDA, scoping of dataset/feature, identify audit owners.
Week 1: Networking & KMS proof-of-concept (private peering or peered VPC).
Week 2-3: Small production-like traffic with monitoring enabled (no sensitive PII unless redacted).
Week 4: Evidence collection run: collect logs, manifests, and signed audit snapshots; hand to buyer audit team.
Week 5: Performance verification, failover test (simulate region or instance loss).
Week 6: Review outcomes, iterate on SLOs, propose contract appendix for runbook and migration SLA.

Sample short email template to CISO (editable):
Subject: Short pilot proposal — private inference on your VPC (6-week, evidence-first)
Hi <Name>,
We’d like to propose a scoped 6-week pilot to demonstrate inference within your private network with KMS integration and a full evidence handover for your auditors. Objective: verify latency SLO, show immutable audit trails, and validate migration/export mechanics. Can we schedule a 30-minute architecture review?
Thanks,
Priya (on behalf of Redwood Solutions)

Contract and procurement levers (what to offer when negotiating):
- Evidence binder + acceptance criteria tied to pilot deliverables (reduce ambiguity).
- Migration assistance credit (X hours) in case of termination.
- Optional on-prem deployment fee vs managed private control plane (pricing split).
- Defined breach notification SLA and indemnities scoped to customer data processed by the deployment.

Open/unstable questions (for product/legal to decide quickly):
- Default incident notification SLA for private-managed control plane (we need standard days/hours).
- Template language for export formats (structure of model + KV cache) and whether we certify migration test for each major model family.
- Standard retention windows for audit logs in private deployments (we should propose 365 days but allow negotiation).

Field notes / heuristics from recent calls:
- Auditors repeatedly ask for a small 'evidence demo' not just a report — walking them through signed manifests on a call is highly persuasive.
- Finance buyers care more about predictability and the ability to cap spend than raw per-token price; surface reserved capacity and burst controls in commercial conversations.
- Many customers are willing to accept a managed control plane if keys + logs remain customer-owned and there is a clear export path.

Quick checklists (for AE before demo):
- Have KMS contacts been introduced? Y/N
- Has legal seen the pilot acceptance criteria? Y/N
- Are we offering a migration credit in the proposal? Y/N

Next steps (immediate cadence for GT team):
- Iterate this doc with Legal to finalize recommended SLA templates (owner: Sara Bloom).
- Package a 2-slide "Evidence Demo" kit for SEs with screenshots and scripts (owner: Jae Park).
- Create a small Confluence page with completed pilot worksheets and link from sales play docs (referenced in CONFS-1123).

References: CONFS-1123 (evidence binder pattern), JIRA-GT-4892 (pilot worksheet), PR#78 (private-deploy-playbook updates).

Notes to self / seller tips: keep scripts short, lead with evidence, and get auditors a live walkthrough — it closes deals faster than an SSO PDF.
